context: US county choropleth showing election margins and swing across 5 election years (2008-2024), with a linked histogram of swing distribution and a brush-to-highlight interaction; year is controlled via a slider with a play button.
first_impression: The map failed to render in the screenshot — both the choropleth canvas and histogram panel are blank, showing only the title, D+30/R+30 legend labels, and slider controls, strongly suggesting the async TopoJSON fetch did not complete before capture.
what_works: Cognitively lean design: only 2 linked views (map + histogram) with a diverging 2-hue red/blue scale eliminates color overload; brush-to-highlight with alpha fadeout (0.08 for unselected counties) is a clean mechanic that would preserve spatial context while isolating a swing range.
what_doesnt: The rendering failure makes perceptual evaluation impossible and is itself a UX failure — no loading indicator or fallback means the viewer sees a blank screen with no explanation; year transitions use instant full-canvas redraws with no animation, so when the play mode cycles counties the viewer has no object constancy cue to track which regions changed.
